# External Agent Builder

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module

## Available Commands

| Command | Skill file | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

## How to Use

When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":

1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.

## Tool Mapping (Codex)

The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:

| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |

## Protocol Spec

The external agent protocol is defined at:
`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

# External Agent Builder

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module

## Available Commands

| Command | Skill file | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

## How to Use

When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":

1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.

## Tool Mapping (Codex)

The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:

| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |

## Protocol Spec

The external agent protocol is defined at:
`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

# Match the task scope
The user's request sets the scope of your work. Adapt your behavior to what they asked for:

- **Planning**: produce a plan and stop. Do not start editing files. If you spot a decision that needs the user's input, surface it rather than resolving it yourself.
- **Review**: review the code and report findings. Do not fix things yourself unless asked. The analysis is the deliverable.
- **Investigation**: investigate and report findings. Do not make changes unless the task explicitly asks for it.
- **Implementation**: carry the task through to a correct, verified result. This is the default when the user asks you to build, fix, or implement something.

When in doubt about whether to act or ask, ask. A user who asked you to plan or review does not want you to start editing.

# Act, don't over-think
When the task is implementation, your thinking shares the same response budget as your output. Long deliberation can burn the whole budget before you produce anything, and a turn that thinks to the limit and emits no tool call is a wasted turn. So:

- Think in short bursts, then act. Prefer issuing a tool call over more analysis. One probe teaches you more than a long chain of speculation.
- Do not re-read the same file or re-derive the same conclusion twice. Write findings to your scratchpad instead of re-establishing them.
- Explore just enough to act correctly, then stop exploring and do the work.

**Low 1 (01M7P86FCAPB) — parseKeyValue doesn't strip trailing comments**
REAL: `type = "command" # entire` → value parsed as `"command" # entire` (the raw string after trim doesn't unquote) → entryIsCommandType fails → duplicate entries on next install; `command = "..." # note` → rewrites every install dropping the comment. Fix: in parseKeyValue, strip an unquoted `#` comment AFTER the closing quote (or after a closing quote or end of value). Careful: `command = "value # inside"` — the # is INSIDE quotes → keep. Implementation: find the closing quote of the value if it starts with a quote, then cut at the first `#` after it. If the value is unquoted (numbers, bools), cut at the first ` #`. Simple scanner: if value starts with `"` or `'`, find the matching closing quote, then cut everything from the first `#` after it; else cut from the first `#`.

Given uncertainty about entire's idempotency, the conservative fix: emit type 4 on PostCompact only; PreCompact → nil (not forwarded). Practical: drop bare "500"/"429"/"503" substring matches, keep word-level phrases. The e2e restart-on-transient is a nicety; false negatives (missed real transient) just fail the test honestly. Fix: remove bare numeric matches; keep "overloaded", "rate limit", "429" → hmm. Actually simplest robust: match `(?:^|\W)(429|500|503)(?:\W|$)` word-boundary-ish... a port like ":500" would still match \W boundaries. Screen-level matching is inherently fuzzy. The suggestion: "Match on sarvam's actual error banners or anchored HTTP status phrases" — sarvam's API errors show like "ERROR ... 429 Too Many Requests" presumably. Use anchored phrases: "429 too many requests", "rate limit", "overloaded", "503 service unavailable", "500 internal server error", "econnreset", "etimedout", "operation timed out", "deadline exceeded". I'll implement that.

**Low 4 (01M7MH1QHEJ8) — CalculateTokens counts a torn final line**
REAL: the scanner counts the final unterminated line while readRolloutLines excludes it → the same record counted again next time. Fix: skip the final line when the transcript doesn't end with a newline. My CalculateTokens uses bufio.Scanner — I can detect: read all bytes? The transcript is in memory ([]byte) — check `len(transcript) > 0 && transcript[len-1] != '\n'` → the last line is unterminated → skip it. Simple: track whether the scanner's final token was terminated... easier: bytes.HasSuffix(transcript, []byte("\n")) — if false, decrement the line count... actually simplest: pre-compute total lines excluding a torn tail, then only process lines up to that count. Implementation: iterate with index; after the loop, if the data doesn't end with \n, the LAST scanned line is torn → drop its contribution. Track the last-line usage separately and subtract... cleaner: compute `lineCount` first via the same rule as readRolloutLines (number of complete lines = number of '\n'), and stop processing when index reaches that. Let me restructure: completeLines := bytes.Count(transcript, []byte("\n")) — the number of terminated lines... wait no: count of \n IS the number of complete lines (every complete line ends with one; a torn tail has no trailing \n). So process scanner lines with index <= completeLines... hmm, scanner yields completeLines + (1 if torn tail). Skip index > completeLines. That aligns exactly with readRolloutLines' semantics.

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

# External Agent Builder

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module

## Available Commands

| Command | Skill file | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

## How to Use

When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":

1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.

## Tool Mapping (Codex)

The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:

| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |

## Protocol Spec

The external agent protocol is defined at:
`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

```go
// stripTrailingComment removes an unquoted # comment from a value.
func stripTrailingComment(value string) string {
	inQuote := false
	for i := 0; i < len(value); i++ {
		switch value[i] {
		case '\\':
			if inQuote {
				i++ // skip escaped char inside quotes
			}
		case '"':
			inQuote = !inQuote
		case '#':
			if !inQuote {
				return strings.TrimRight(value[:i], " \t")
			}
		}
	}
	return value
}
```

```go
// stripTrailingComment removes an unquoted # comment from a value.
func stripTrailingComment(value string) string {
	inQuote := false
	for i := 0; i < len(value); i++ {
		switch value[i] {
		case '\\':
			if inQuote {
				i++ // skip escaped char inside quotes
			}
		case '"':
			inQuote = !inQuote
		case '#':
			if !inQuote {
				return strings.TrimRight(value[:i], " \t")
			}
		}
	}
	return value
}
```

L21: // back from them. A byte offset here would re-count nearly the whole
L22: // transcript on every checkpoint, so lines (complete and placeholder alike)
L23: // are skipped by index, keeping the alignment the analyzer guarantees.
L24: func (a *Agent) CalculateTokens(transcript []byte, offset int) (protocol.TokenUsageResponse, error) {

L26: 		CacheCreationTokens: 0,
L27: 		SubagentTokens:      nil,
L28: 	}

L34: 		index++

L285: // array of one matcher group, keeping the author's entries.
L286: func repairParentlessHooks(blocks []tomlBlock) []tomlBlock {
L287: 	out := make([]tomlBlock, 0, len(blocks)+len(hookSpecs))
L288: 	seenGroup := map[string]bool{}
L289: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L290: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L291: 		if event != "" && kind == kindHooks && !seenGroup[event] {
L292: 			if isManagedEvent(event) {
L293: 				out = append(out, tomlBlock{header: fmt.Sprintf("[[hooks.%s]]", event)})

L295: 				// parentless entry of the event joins it. Without this
L296: 				// mark, a second parentless entry would get its own
L297: 				// header and silently split the user's entries into
L298: 				// separate matcher groups.
L299: 				seenGroup[event] = true
L300: 			}
L301: 		}
L302: 		if event != "" && kind == "group" {
L303: 			seenGroup[event] = true
L304: 		}
L305: 		out = append(out, block)
L306: 	}
L307: 	return out
L308: }

L310: func isManagedEvent(event string) bool {
L311: 	for _, spec := range hookSpecs {
L312: 		if spec.SarvamEvent == event {
L313: 			return true
L314: 		}
L315: 	}
L316: 	return false
L317: }

L319: // checkNoMapFormEvents rejects the single-bracket map form for events we
L320: // manage. Appending an array-of-tables next to a table definition is a TOML
L321: // type conflict; failing loudly beats corrupting a config the user must fix
L322: // by hand anyway.
L323: func checkNoMapFormEvents(blocks []tomlBlock) error {
L324: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L325: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L326: 		if event != "" && kind == "group" && isManagedEvent(event) && !strings.HasPrefix(block.header, "[[") {

L329: 	}
L330: 	return nil
L331: }

L333: // upsertHookEntries installs the given entries, returning how many hook
L334: // handlers were added or updated. Unrelated config content is untouched.
L335: func upsertHookEntries(path string, entries []configHookEntry, force bool) (int, error) {
L336: 	blocks, err := loadBlocks(path)
L337: 	if err != nil {
L338: 		return 0, err
L339: 	}
L340: 	if err := checkNoMapFormEvents(blocks); err != nil {
L341: 		return 0, err
L342: 	}
L343: 	if force {
L344: 		blocks = dropEntireEntries(blocks)
L345: 	}
L346: 	blocks = repairParentlessHooks(blocks)
L347: 
L348: 	count := 0
L349: 	for _, entry := range entries {
L350: 		if upsertOne(&blocks, entry) {
L351: 			count++
L352: 		}
L353: 	}
L354: 	if count == 0 {
L355: 		return 0, nil
L356: 	}
L357: 	if err := saveBlocks(path, blocks); err != nil {
L358: 		return 0, err
L359: 	}
L360: 	return count, nil
L361: }
L362: 
L363: func upsertOne(blocks *[]tomlBlock, entry configHookEntry) bool {
L364: 	// Update in place when an owned entry exists.
L365: 	for i, block := range *blocks {
L366: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L367: 		if event != entry.Event || kind != kindHooks {
L368: 			continue
L369: 		}
L370: 		if !isEntireEntry(block) {
L371: 			continue
L372: 		}
L373: 		if entryCommand(block) == entry.Command {
L374: 			return false
L375: 		}
L376: 		for j, line := range block.body {
L377: 			if key, _, ok := parseKeyValue(line); ok && key == "command" {
L378: 				(*blocks)[i].body[j] = "command = " + encodeTOMLString(entry.Command)
L379: 				return true
L380: 			}
L381: 		}
L382: 	}
L383: 
L384: 	// Insert after the event's last hook entry when one exists; otherwise
L385: 	// open a fresh group at the end of the hooks region (or EOF).
L386: 	insertAt := -1
L387: 	lastHooksRegion := -1
L388: 	for i, block := range *blocks {
L389: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L390: 		if event == "" {
L391: 			continue
L392: 		}
L393: 		if kind == kindHooks && event == entry.Event {
L394: 			insertAt = i + 1
L395: 		}
L396: 		if strings.HasPrefix(block.header, "[hooks.") || strings.HasPrefix(block.header, "[[hooks.") {
L397: 			lastHooksRegion = i + 1
L398: 		}
L399: 	}
L400: 	at := len(*blocks)
L401: 	if insertAt >= 0 {
L402: 		at = insertAt
L403: 	} else if lastHooksRegion >= 0 {
L404: 		at = lastHooksRegion
L405: 	}
L406: 	newBlocks := newEntryBlocks(entry.Event, entry.Command)
L407: 	out := make([]tomlBlock, 0, len(*blocks)+len(newBlocks))
L408: 	out = append(out, (*blocks)[:at]...)
L409: 	out = append(out, newBlocks...)
L410: 	out = append(out, (*blocks)[at:]...)
L411: 	*blocks = out
L412: 	return true
L413: }

L415: // removeHookEntries deletes every entry this adapter owns.
L416: func removeHookEntries(path string) error {
L417: 	blocks, err := loadBlocks(path)
L418: 	if err != nil {
L419: 		return err
L420: 	}

L422: 		return nil // no config at all
L423: 	}
L424: 	kept := dropEntireEntries(blocks)

L428: 
L429: func dropEntireEntries(blocks []tomlBlock) []tomlBlock {
L430: 	out := make([]tomlBlock, 0, len(blocks))
L431: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L432: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L433: 		if event != "" && kind == kindHooks && isEntireEntry(block) {
L434: 			continue
L435: 		}
L436: 		out = append(out, block)
L437: 	}
L438: 	return out

L441: // dropEmptyManagedGroups removes [[hooks.<Event>]] group headers for our
L442: // events once the event has no hook entries left at all. A group that still
L443: // carries content (a matcher, foreign entries) always stays.
L444: func dropEmptyManagedGroups(blocks []tomlBlock) []tomlBlock {
L445: 	eventsWithEntries := map[string]bool{}
L446: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L447: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L448: 		if event != "" && kind == kindHooks {
L449: 			eventsWithEntries[event] = true
L450: 		}
L451: 	}
L452: 	out := make([]tomlBlock, 0, len(blocks))
L453: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L454: 		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L455: 		if event != "" && kind == "group" && isManagedEvent(event) &&
L456: 			len(block.body) == 0 && !eventsWithEntries[event] {
L457: 			continue
L458: 		}
L459: 		out = append(out, block)
L460: 	}
L461: 	return out
L462: }

L464: func hookEntryInstalled(path, event, command string) bool {
L465: 	blocks, err := loadBlocks(path)
L466: 	if err != nil {
L467: 		return false
L468: 	}
L469: 	blocks = repairParentlessHooks(blocks)
L470: 	for _, block := range blocks {
L471: 		e, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
L472: 		if e != event || kind != kindHooks {
L473: 			continue
L474: 		}
L475: 		if isEntireEntry(block) && entryCommand(block) == command {
L476: 			return true
L477: 		}
L478: 	}

L482: func loadBlocks(path string) ([]tomlBlock, error) {
L483: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
L484: 	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
L485: 		return []tomlBlock{{}}, nil
L486: 	}
L487: 	if err != nil {
L488: 		return nil, err
L489: 	}
L490: 	if len(strings.TrimSpace(string(data))) == 0 {
L491: 		return []tomlBlock{{}}, nil
L492: 	}
L493: 	return parseConfigBlocks(string(data)), nil
L494: }

L496: func saveBlocks(path string, blocks []tomlBlock) error {
L497: 	content := serializeConfigBlocks(blocks)
L498: 	// filepath.Dir is separator-aware: on Windows the config path carries
L499: 	// backslashes, where a hand-rolled "/" split would return "." and leave
L500: 	// the .sarvam directory uncreated.
L501: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o750); err != nil {
L502: 		return err

Now I have the full config.go picture. Let me plan the two config fixes:

**Fix 1: parseKeyValue strips unquoted trailing comments (finding 01M7P86FCAPB).**

Current parseKeyValue takes the raw value after `=`. With `type = "command" # entire`, the value seen is `"command" # entire` — the quote-stripping check `value[0]=='"' && value[len-1]=='"'` fails (ends with "entire"), so value stays raw → `entryIsCommandType` returns false (value != "command") → owned entry not recognized → duplicates on next install. With `command = "..." # note`, isEntireEntry matches via Contains, but command never equals the expected string → every install rewrites and drops the comment.

Fix: strip a trailing comment before decoding. Quote-aware: a `#` inside a quoted string is not a comment. The finding says: "Strip an unquoted # comment after a closing quote before decoding."

Implementation: a helper that scans the value: track quote state ('"' and '\''), and escaped chars inside basic strings; find the first '#' that is outside quotes → truncate there. Then TrimRight the remainder of whitespace.

```go
// stripTrailingComment removes an unquoted TOML comment from a value: a '#'
// outside any quoted string ends the value. Quoted '#' characters survive.
func stripTrailingComment(value string) string {
	var quote byte
	for i := 0; i < len(value); i++ {
		ch := value[i]
		switch {
		case quote != 0:
			if ch == '\\' && quote == '"' && i+1 < len(value) {
				i++ // skip the escaped character
				continue
			}
			if ch == quote {
				quote = 0
			}
		case ch == '"' || ch == '\'':
			quote = ch
		case ch == '#':
			return strings.TrimRight(value[:i], " \t")
		}
	}
	return value
}
```

This mirrors netBracketsOutsideQuotes's quote handling. Then in parseKeyValue:

```go
	value = strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[eq+1:])
	value = strings.TrimSpace(stripTrailingComment(value))
```

Wait — order: strip comment first, then trim. stripTrailingComment returns value[:i] right-trimmed; then TrimSpace handles any leading. Fine either way. Actually one nuance: the key part could also carry a comment before '='? `key = value # comment` — the comment comes after value. Also `# key = value` (comment line) is already handled by the HasPrefix("#") check.

Edge: `command = "run # now"` → quote tracking: at i of '"' quote opens; '#' inside quote → skipped. Good.

Edge: `command = 'x#y'` — literal string, '#' inside survives. Good.

Edge: value like `command = "a" # b` → at closing '"' quote=0, then ' ' skipped, '#' at outside → truncate → value = `"a"` → decodes to `a`. 

Edge: unquoted `timeout = 30 # seconds` → truncate at '#' → `30`. Good.

Now also `parseKeyValue` is used by entryCommand, entryIsCommandType. With comments stripped, `type = "command" # entire` now decodes value = "command" → entryIsCommandType true → isEntireEntry works → no duplicate install. And `command = "..." # note` decodes to the exact command string → `entryCommand(block) == entry.Command` → upsertOne returns false (already installed, unchanged) → comment preserved (no rewrite). 

**Fix 2: force path leaves empty managed groups (findings 01M7MH1QHX5A + 01M7P868AZDG).**

In upsertHookEntries with force=true: `blocks = dropEntireEntries(blocks)` removes owned entries, leaving behind the `[[hooks.<Event>]]` group headers we added (newEntryBlocks adds a group header + entry header). Then repairParentlessHooks... then upsertOne inserts. upsertOne's insert path: "Insert after the event's last hook entry when one exists; otherwise open a fresh group at the end of the hooks region (or EOF)". After dropEntireEntries, there are no `.hooks` entries for the event → insertAt stays -1 → opens a FRESH group at the end of the hooks region → the old now-empty group header remains → accumulation: each force install adds one more empty group header.

Wait — but force install runs `dropEntireEntries` then upserts each entry — each upsertOne call inserts `newEntryBlocks` (a fresh `[[hooks.Event]]` group + the `[[hooks.Event.hooks]]` entry). So after force, the config has: old empty group header + new group + new entry. Second force: drops entries, keeps both group headers (old empty + the one from first force), then inserts ANOTHER group+entry. Etc. Accumulation. That's the finding.

Fix per handoff: "dropEmptyManagedGroups also drops empty managed group headers not followed by a same-event .hooks entry; call it from the force path".

Look at dropEmptyManagedGroups current logic: it computes eventsWithEntries over ALL blocks (any `.hooks` entry header for the event), and drops empty managed groups for events with NO entries anywhere. In the force path, after dropEntireEntries, the event has no entries → eventsWithEntries[event] false → all empty managed groups for the event get dropped. Then upsertOne inserts fresh group+entry. 

So actually the CURRENT dropEmptyManagedGroups would handle the force path fine! The handoff says "dropEmptyManagedGroups also drops empty managed group headers not followed by a same-event .hooks entry" — hmm, why "also"? Let me re-read the finding fragment I saw: "01M7P868AZDG medium ... therefore leaves another empty [[hooks.X]] group in the user's config. Either drop the now-empty managed groups after dropEntireEntries (as removeHookEntries does with dropEmptyManagedGroups), or have the insert reuse the existing empty group." — that's 01M7MH1QHX5A (low) per the tail. 01M7P868AZDG (medium) is fully elided for me. Its subject: "empty group headers". Hmm.

The handoff's exact next step for config.go: "dropEmptyManagedGroups also drops empty managed group headers not followed by a same-event .hooks entry; call it from the force path". So the requirement is:

(a) call dropEmptyManagedGroups from the force path after dropEntireEntries (upsertHookEntries), AND
(b) extend dropEmptyManagedGroups so an empty managed group header is dropped even when the event DOES have entries elsewhere — i.e., a group is kept only if a `.hooks` entry for the same event FOLLOWS it.

Case (b): uninstall-with-foreign-entry scenario. Suppose the user's config:

```toml
[[hooks.SessionStart]]
matcher = "foo"   # user's group with matcher

[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]  # user's foreign entry
command = "their-thing"
```

Plus our entries somewhere. After uninstall (dropEntireEntries), the user's group and entry remain — dropEmptyManagedGroups keeps the user's group (has body matcher). Fine.

But consider: our group `[[hooks.SessionStart]]` (empty, we created it) followed LATER by the user's own `[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]` entry. Current dropEmptyManagedGroups: eventsWithEntries[SessionStart] = true (user's entry exists!) → our empty group is KEPT even though our entry is gone. That's the (b) case: "empty managed group headers not followed by a same-event .hooks entry" — hmm, but "not followed by a same-event entry" — in this scenario the user's entry DOES follow (later in the file). Hmm.

Wait, let me re-think what "followed by a same-event .hooks entry" means. Blocks are sequential. Our inserted layout is:

```toml
[[hooks.X]]        <- group header (ours, empty body)
[[hooks.X.hooks]]  <- entry
type = "command"
command = "..."
```

An empty managed group that is IMMEDIATELY followed by its `.hooks` entry is the normal pairing (keep it — the group is the parent of the entry). An empty managed group NOT followed by a same-event entry is an orphan (drop it).

So the refined rule: drop an empty managed group header unless the NEXT block (or a subsequent block before any other header for a different... hmm) is a `.hooks` entry of the same event? Or: keep a group if a same-event entry follows it before another same-event group header appears?

Scenario for 01M7P868AZDG (install/replaces leaves empty groups — "Medium"): Consider install when config has our entries from a previous version (different command), plus... hmm. Actually let me think about the scenario where the CURRENT logic fails and the "followed by" logic is needed:

1. User has their own group: `[[hooks.Stop]]` with body matcher, then their foreign `.hooks` entry.
2. We install: upsertOne — no owned entry exists → insert path: insertAt = -1... wait, their `.hooks` entry exists for the event so insertAt = i+1 (after their entry) — actually the loop sets insertAt to the LAST same-event kindHooks block index+1. So our newEntryBlocks (fresh group + our entry) insert AFTER the user's entry. Config:

```toml
[[hooks.Stop]]
matcher = "..."

[[hooks.Stop.hooks]]     # user's
command = "their"

[[hooks.Stop]]           # ours (empty group)
[[hooks.Stop.hooks]]     # ours
command = "entire hooks sarvam ..."
```

Fine — our group is immediately followed by our entry. Uninstall: dropEntireEntries removes our entry; dropEmptyManagedGroups: eventsWithEntries[Stop]=true (user's entry) → our empty group KEPT → leftover empty group in user config! That's a leak the current uninstall leaves. The "followed by same-event entry" rule fixes it: our empty group is followed by... the next block. After removal, next block after our empty group is whatever follows — nothing (EOF). Not followed by same-event entry → drop. And the user's group (has matcher body) stays regardless.

But careful — the "followed by" rule must not drop a group when the entry follows non-adjacently? In TOML array-of-tables, `[[hooks.Stop]]` then `[[hooks.Stop.hooks]]` — the entry belongs to the LAST group opened for that event. If between them there's another `[[hooks.Stop]]` header, the entry belongs to the later one. So adjacency is the right criterion: an entry block's parent group is the immediately preceding same-event group header.

But what about `[[hooks.X]]` group followed by `[[hooks.Y.hooks]]` (different event) then `[[hooks.X.hooks]]`? Malformed-ish; sarvam would attach the X entry... to nothing (it would create/attach per TOML rules — actually in TOML, `[[hooks.Y.hooks]]` after `[[hooks.X]]` — array-of-tables X gets closed; X.hooks entry creates its own. The preceding group adjacency is the practical convention.)

Simpler robust rule: keep an empty managed group iff the immediately-next block is a `.hooks` entry of the same event. Non-empty managed groups (matchers) always stay. Foreign/other headers always stay.

Hmm wait — but there's a subtlety with the user's group WITHOUT matcher body:

```toml
[[hooks.SessionStart]]
[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]   # user's foreign entry
command = "their"
```

(the sarvam docs' shape — group header with empty body directly followed by entry). Is that group "managed"? isManagedEvent(event) is true (SessionStart is one of our five events) — but the group belongs to the USER (their entry follows it). Under the adjacency rule: group is followed by a same-event `.hooks` entry → KEPT. Good — we only drop empty groups whose adjacent next block is NOT a same-event entry.

Uninstall scenario with our + user's entries:
```toml
[[hooks.SessionStart]]          # user's group (empty body!)
[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]    # user's foreign entry
command = "their"
[[hooks.SessionStart]]          # our group
[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]    # our entry (dropped on uninstall)
command = "entire..."
```
After dropEntireEntries:
```toml
[[hooks.SessionStart]]           # user's — followed by user's entry → keep
[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]] command = "their"
[[hooks.SessionStart]]           # ours — followed by EOF → drop
```
The adjacency rule drops only ours. 

Force-install accumulation scenario:
```toml
[[hooks.SessionStart]]   # ours from previous force
[[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]] + entry  (dropped by dropEntireEntries in force)
```
Force: dropEntireEntries leaves the empty group; then... if we call dropEmptyManagedGroups right after dropEntireEntries (before repair/upserts), the empty group is followed by EOF → dropped. Then upsert inserts a fresh group+entry. Net: exactly one group + one entry per event. Repeated force: always ends with exactly one group header per event. 

But WAIT — the handoff said call it from the force path. Where exactly? In upsertHookEntries:

```go
if force {
    blocks = dropEntireEntries(blocks)
    blocks = dropEmptyManagedGroups(blocks)   // NEW
}
```

Hmm — but should it run on non-force installs too? If not force, upsertOne updates in place or inserts after last entry; an orphaned empty group (from an ancient bug or a manual edit) would remain — but that's pre-existing user content, we shouldn't touch it on plain install. Force = "make it exactly ours, clean" → cleaning is right. Uninstall already calls it. Good: force + uninstall.

Now — is the CURRENT dropEmptyManagedGroups' eventsWithEntries global-check wrong under the adjacency rule? Replace the global check with adjacency:

```go
// dropEmptyManagedGroups removes [[hooks.<Event>]] group headers for our
// managed events that no longer parent any hook entry: an empty group is
// kept only when a same-event [[hooks.<Event>.hooks]] entry immediately
// follows it. A group that still carries content (a matcher) always stays,
// and foreign events are never touched.
func dropEmptyManagedGroups(blocks []tomlBlock) []tomlBlock {
	out := make([]tomlBlock, 0, len(blocks))
	for i, block := range blocks {
		event, kind := headerEvent(block.header)
		if event != "" && kind == "group" && isManagedEvent(event) && len(block.body) == 0 {
			if !followedBySameEventEntry(blocks, i) {
				continue
			}
		}
		out = append(out, block)
	}
	return out
}

func followedBySameEventEntry(blocks []tomlBlock, groupIndex int) bool {
	if groupIndex+1 >= len(blocks) {
		return false
	}
	event, kind := headerEvent(blocks[groupIndex+1].header)
	groupEvent, _ := headerEvent(blocks[groupIndex].header)
	return event == groupEvent && kind == kindHooks
}

// stripTrailingComment removes an unquoted TOML comment from a value: a '#'
// outside any quoted string ends the value. Quoted '#' characters survive.
func stripTrailingComment(value string) string {
	var quote byte
	for i := 0; i < len(value); i++ {
		ch := value[i]
		switch {
		case quote != 0:
			if ch == '\\' && quote == '"' && i+1 < len(value) {
				i++ // skip the escaped character
				continue
			}
			if ch == quote {
				quote = 0
			}
		case ch == '"' || ch == '\'':
			quote = ch
		case ch == '#':

		}
	}
	return value

L64: func TestRepairParentlessHooks_SingleGroupForAllEntries(t *testing.T) {
L65: 	// Several parentless hook entries for one event must be repaired with a
L66: 	// single synthetic group header, so they stay one matcher group — a
L67: 	// header per entry would silently split the user's entries.
L68: 	content := `[hooks]
L69: [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]
L70: type = "command"
L71: command = "/usr/local/bin/first-start-hook"
L72: [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]
L73: type = "command"
L74: command = "/usr/local/bin/second-start-hook"
L75: [[hooks.UserPromptSubmit.hooks]]
L76: type = "command"
L77: command = "/usr/local/bin/prompt-hook"
L78: `
L79: 	repaired := serializeConfigBlocks(repairParentlessHooks(parseConfigBlocks(content)))
L80: 
L81: 	if strings.Count(repaired, "[[hooks.SessionStart]]\n") != 1 {
L82: 		t.Fatalf("exactly one synthetic SessionStart group header may be inserted, got:\n%s", repaired)
L83: 	}
L84: 	if strings.Count(repaired, "[[hooks.UserPromptSubmit]]\n") != 1 {
L85: 		t.Fatalf("exactly one synthetic UserPromptSubmit group header may be inserted, got:\n%s", repaired)
L86: 	}
L87: 	for _, want := range []string{
L88: 		`command = "/usr/local/bin/first-start-hook"`,
L89: 		`command = "/usr/local/bin/second-start-hook"`,
L90: 		`command = "/usr/local/bin/prompt-hook"`,
L91: 	} {
L92: 		if !strings.Contains(repaired, want) {
L93: 			t.Errorf("entries lost during repair, missing %q:\n%s", want, repaired)
L94: 		}
L95: 	}
L96: 
L97: 	// The end-to-end install must not add a second synthetic header for the
L98: 	// user's entries on top of the repair: our own entry opens its own new
L99: 	// group, so exactly two headers exist in total.
L100: 	path := writeConfig(t, content)
L101: 	if _, err := upsertHookEntries(path, testEntries(), false); err != nil {
L102: 		t.Fatal(err)
L103: 	}
L104: 	installed := readConfig(t, path)
L105: 	if got := strings.Count(installed, "[[hooks.SessionStart]]\n"); got != 2 {
L106: 		t.Fatalf("installed config should carry the repaired group plus ours, got %d headers:\n%s", got, installed)
L107: 	}
L108: }

L179: func TestInstallHooks_MatcherScopedForeignGroup(t *testing.T) {
L180: 	// A user's matcher-scoped group for one of our events must not capture
L181: 	// our entry: the installer always opens its own matcher-less group, so
L182: 	// the hook fires for every event, not only where the foreign matcher hits.
L183: 	path := writeConfig(t, `[[hooks.SessionStart]]
L184: matcher = "SomeTool"
L185: 
L186: [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]
L187: type = "command"
L188: command = "/usr/local/bin/user-start-hook"
L189: `)
L190: 
L191: 	if _, err := upsertHookEntries(path, testEntries(), false); err != nil {
L192: 		t.Fatal(err)
L193: 	}
L194: 	content := readConfig(t, path)
L195: 
L196: 	first := strings.Index(content, "[[hooks.SessionStart]]")
L197: 	second := strings.Index(content[first+1:], "[[hooks.SessionStart]]") + first + 1
L198: 	ours := strings.Index(content, "entire hooks sarvam session-start")
L199: 	if first >= second || second >= ours {
L200: 		t.Fatalf("our entry must open its own group after the user's, got:\n%s", content)
L201: 	}
L202: 	if strings.Count(content, "matcher") != 1 {
L203: 		t.Errorf("the user's matcher must stay in their group only:\n%s", content)
L204: 	}
L205: 	if !strings.Contains(content, `command = "/usr/local/bin/user-start-hook"`) {
L206: 		t.Errorf("the user's entry must be preserved:\n%s", content)
L207: 	}
L208: }

L66: 		return input.SessionID
L67: 	}

L71: // sarvamHome resolves $SARVAM_HOME, defaulting to ~/.sarvam.
L72: func sarvamHome() string {
L73: 	if v := os.Getenv("SARVAM_HOME"); v != "" {
L74: 		return v
L75: 	}
L76: 	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
L77: 	if err != nil {
L78: 		return ".sarvam"
L79: 	}
L80: 	return filepath.Join(home, ".sarvam")
L81: }
L82: 
L83: // GetSessionDir returns where sarvam keeps the sessions it is writing today.
L84: // The rollout store is date-partitioned (sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/), and callers
L85: // — including Entire's session discovery — read the directory
L86: // non-recursively, so the day directory is the useful answer, not the root.
L87: func (a *Agent) GetSessionDir(repoPath string) (string, error) {
L88: 	_ = repoPath // kept for interface symmetry; the store is global
L89: 	return filepath.Join(sarvamHome(), "sessions", time.Now().Format("2006/01/02")), nil
L90: }
L91: 
L92: // ResolveSessionFile maps a session ID to its native rollout JSONL when one
L93: // exists, and to a deterministic in-store path otherwise. The fallback keeps
L94: // read/write-session round-trips stable without ever touching a native
L95: // transcript that exists on disk.
L96: func (a *Agent) ResolveSessionFile(sessionDir, sessionID string) string {
L97: 	if strings.TrimSpace(sessionDir) == "" {
L98: 		sessionDir, _ = a.GetSessionDir("")
L99: 	}
L100: 	if id := strings.TrimSpace(sessionID); id != "" {
L101: 		if path := findRolloutFile(sessionDir, id); path != "" {
L102: 			return path
L103: 		}
L104: 	}
L105: 	return filepath.Join(sessionDir, safeFilename(sessionID)+".jsonl")
L106: }
L107: 
L108: // findRolloutFile searches for the rollout file whose name ends with the
L109: // thread ID, returning the newest match. The given directory is searched
L110: // first — both directly (the day directory GetSessionDir returns) and
L111: // date-partitioned three levels deep (the sessions root older callers pass) —
L112: // and then the whole sessions store, because a session still running from an
L113: // earlier day lives outside today's day directory and must not fall back to
L114: // the synthetic path.
L115: func findRolloutFile(sessionDir, sessionID string) string {
L116: 	safe := safeFilename(sessionID)
L117: 	if safe == "" || safe == stubSessionID {
L118: 		return ""
L119: 	}
L120: 	patterns := []string{
L121: 		filepath.Join(sessionDir, "rollout-*-"+safe+".jsonl"),
L122: 		filepath.Join(sessionDir, "*", "*", "*", "rollout-*-"+safe+".jsonl"),
L123: 	}
L124: 	if root := filepath.Join(sarvamHome(), "sessions"); root != sessionDir {
L125: 		patterns = append(patterns, filepath.Join(root, "*", "*", "*", "rollout-*-"+safe+".jsonl"))
L126: 	}
L127: 	var matches []string
L128: 	for _, pattern := range patterns {
L129: 		found, err := filepath.Glob(pattern)
L130: 		if err == nil {
L131: 			matches = append(matches, found...)
L132: 		}
L133: 	}
L134: 	if len(matches) == 0 {
L135: 		return ""
L136: 	}
L137: 	sort.Strings(matches) // date-prefixed names sort chronologically
L138: 	return matches[len(matches)-1]
L139: }
L140: 
L141: func (a *Agent) FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string {
L142: 	if strings.TrimSpace(sessionID) == "" {
L143: 		return "sarvam-code resume --last"
L144: 	}
L145: 	return "sarvam-code resume " + shellQuote(sessionID)
L146: }
L147: 
L148: func shellQuote(value string) string {
L149: 	if value == "" {
L150: 		return "''"
L151: 	}
L152: 	if strings.IndexFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
L153: 		return !isSafeShellQuoteRune(r)
L154: 	}) == -1 {
L155: 		return value
L156: 	}
L157: 	return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(value, "'", "'\\''") + "'"
L158: }
L159: 
L160: func isSafeShellQuoteRune(r rune) bool {
L161: 	return r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '.' || r == ':' ||
L162: 		(r >= '0' && r <= '9') ||
L163: 		(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') ||
L164: 		(r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z')
L165: }
L166: 
L167: // safeFilename maps a session ID onto a filename-safe string. Session IDs are
L168: // UUIDs in practice, but the protocol accepts any string: common safe
L169: // punctuation is preserved so the ID stays greppable in resolved paths, and
L170: // anything hostile — including Windows reserved device names, which are not
L171: // valid files there even with an extension — collapses to a hash instead of
L172: // reaching the filesystem. Colons are not safe punctuation: they are path
L173: // separators or ADS markers on Windows.
L174: func safeFilename(sessionID string) string {
L175: 	original := strings.TrimSpace(sessionID)
L176: 	if original == "" {
L177: 		return stubSessionID
L178: 	}
L179: 	var b strings.Builder
L180: 	for _, r := range original {
L181: 		switch {
L182: 		case r >= '0' && r <= '9', r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z':
L183: 			b.WriteRune(r)
L184: 		case r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '.':
L185: 			b.WriteRune(r)
L186: 		default:
L187: 			b.WriteByte('_')
L188: 		}
L189: 	}
L190: 	out := strings.Trim(b.String(), "._")
L191: 	if out == "" {
L192: 		return stubSessionID
L193: 	}
L194: 	if out == original && !isWindowsDeviceName(out) {
L195: 		return out
L196: 	}
L197: 	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(original))
L198: 	return fmt.Sprintf("~%x", sum[:16])
L199: }
L200: 
L201: // isWindowsDeviceName reports whether the (already sanitized) name collides
L202: // with a reserved DOS device: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9,
L203: // case-insensitively. Writing "<name>.jsonl" against these is not a real
L204: // file on Windows, so they always take the hashed form.
L205: func isWindowsDeviceName(name string) bool {
L206: 	upper := strings.ToUpper(name)
L207: 	switch upper {
L208: 	case "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL":
L209: 		return true
L210: 	}
L211: 	if len(upper) == 4 {
L212: 		switch {
L213: 		case strings.HasPrefix(upper, "COM") && upper[3] >= '1' && upper[3] <= '9':
L214: 			return true
L215: 		case strings.HasPrefix(upper, "LPT") && upper[3] >= '1' && upper[3] <= '9':
L216: 			return true
L217: 		}
L218: 	}
L219: 	return false
L220: }
L221: 
L222: // sessionIDAndRef picks the session reference for a read: an explicit ref
L223: // wins, then the native rollout for the ID, then the deterministic path.
L224: func (a *Agent) sessionIDAndRef(input *protocol.HookInputJSON) (string, string) {
L225: 	sessionID := stubSessionID
L226: 	if input != nil && strings.TrimSpace(input.SessionID) != "" {
L227: 		sessionID = input.SessionID
L228: 	}
L229: 	if input != nil && strings.TrimSpace(input.SessionRef) != "" {
L230: 		return sessionID, input.SessionRef
L231: 	}
L232: 	return sessionID, a.ResolveSessionFile("", sessionID)
L233: }
L234: 
L235: // ReadSession rebuilds the AgentSession envelope from the transcript at the
L236: // session ref. Native data is the raw rollout JSONL; modified files are
L237: // derived from it on the fly.
L238: func (a *Agent) ReadSession(input *protocol.HookInputJSON) (protocol.AgentSessionJSON, error) {
L239: 	sessionID, sessionRef := a.sessionIDAndRef(input)
L240: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(sessionRef)
L241: 	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
L242: 		data = nil
L243: 	} else if err != nil {
L244: 		return protocol.AgentSessionJSON{}, err
L245: 	}
L246: 	modifiedFiles, _, err := a.ExtractModifiedFiles(sessionRef, 0)
L247: 	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
L248: 		modifiedFiles = nil
L249: 	} else if err != nil {
L250: 		return protocol.AgentSessionJSON{}, err
L251: 	}
L252: 	return protocol.AgentSessionJSON{
L253: 		SessionID:     sessionID,
L254: 		AgentName:     AgentName,
L255: 		RepoPath:      protocol.RepoRoot(),
L256: 		SessionRef:    sessionRef,
L257: 		StartTime:     time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
L258: 		NativeData:    data,
L259: 		ModifiedFiles: modifiedFiles,
L260: 		NewFiles:      []string{},
L261: 		DeletedFiles:  []string{},
L262: 	}, nil
L263: }
L264: 
L265: // WriteSession persists native session bytes at the ref Entire resolved —
L266: // but never into sarvam's own rollout store. A native rollout is sarvam's
L267: // append-only transcript; replacing it with an entire-captured snapshot
L268: // would truncate live appends or clobber history, which redaction cannot
L269: // undo. Rollout-shaped refs are refused outright, an empty payload is not a
L270: // snapshot at all, and an empty ref resolves to the deterministic store path
L271: // rather than ResolveSessionFile, which prefers the native file.
L272: func (a *Agent) WriteSession(session protocol.AgentSessionJSON) error {
L273: 	if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
L274: 		return errEmptySessionData
L275: 	}
L276: 	ref := strings.TrimSpace(session.SessionRef)
L277: 	if ref == "" {
L278: 		if strings.TrimSpace(session.SessionID) == "" {
L279: 			return errMissingSessionRef
L280: 		}
L281: 		ref = a.storePath(session.SessionID)
L282: 	}
L283: 	if isNativeRolloutPath(ref) {
L284: 		return errNativeRolloutWrite
L285: 	}
L286: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(ref), 0o700); err != nil {
L287: 		return err
L288: 	}
L289: 	return os.WriteFile(ref, session.NativeData, 0o600)
L290: }
L291: 
L292: // storePath is the deterministic in-store location for a session ID. It
L293: // deliberately bypasses ResolveSessionFile, which returns the native
L294: // rollout whenever one exists.
L295: func (a *Agent) storePath(sessionID string) string {
L296: 	dir, _ := a.GetSessionDir("")
L297: 	return filepath.Join(dir, safeFilename(sessionID)+".jsonl")
L298: }
L299: 
L300: // isNativeRolloutPath reports whether the path names one of sarvam's own
L301: // rollout transcripts (rollout-<timestamp>-<thread>.jsonl), which write
L302: // targets must never touch.
L303: func isNativeRolloutPath(path string) bool {
L304: 	base := filepath.Base(path)
L305: 	return strings.HasPrefix(base, "rollout-") && strings.HasSuffix(base, ".jsonl")
L306: }
L307: 
L308: // ReadTranscript returns the raw transcript bytes at the ref. Entire runs its
L309: // own redaction over the result and hands a temp copy back through
L310: // compact-transcript for the Entire-facing projection.
L311: func (a *Agent) ReadTranscript(sessionRef string) ([]byte, error) {
L312: 	return os.ReadFile(sessionRef)
L313: }
L314: 
L315: func (a *Agent) ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error) {
L316: 	if maxSize <= 0 {
L317: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("max-size must be positive, got %d", maxSize)
L318: 	}
L319: 	if len(content) == 0 {
L320: 		return [][]byte{{}}, nil
L321: 	}
L322: 	var chunks [][]byte
L323: 	for start := 0; start < len(content); start += maxSize {
L324: 		end := start + maxSize
L325: 		if end > len(content) {
L326: 			end = len(content)
L327: 		}
L328: 		chunk := make([]byte, end-start)
L329: 		copy(chunk, content[start:end])
L330: 		chunks = append(chunks, chunk)
L331: 	}
L332: 	return chunks, nil
L333: }
L334: 
L335: func (a *Agent) ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error) {
L336: 	total := 0
L337: 	for _, chunk := range chunks {
L338: 		total += len(chunk)
L339: 	}
L340: 	out := make([]byte, 0, total)
L341: 	for _, chunk := range chunks {
L342: 		out = append(out, chunk...)
L343: 	}
L344: 	return out, nil
L345: }

L81:     `[hooks.state."<project-config>:<event_snake>:<matcher-idx>:<hook-idx>"]`
L82:     entries with `enabled` and `trusted_hash` (sha256, scheme opaque) to the
L83:     **user** config. Not reproducible offline (brute-forced several
L84:     serializations; no match), so the installer cannot pre-seed it.
L85: 
L86: ## Session Management
L87: 
L88: - Session directory: `$SARVAM_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/` (local start date).
L89:   Override root via `SARVAM_HOME` env. Archived sessions move to
L90:   `$SARVAM_HOME/archived_sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`.
L91: - Session files: one JSONL per run:
L92:   `rollout-<YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss>-<thread_id>.jsonl` where `<thread_id>` is
L93:   the session UUID.
L94: - Session ID source: hook input `session_id` (== thread UUID == the rollout
L95:   filename suffix == `session_meta.payload.id`).
L96: - Session file format: JSONL, one object per line with `timestamp` + `type`:
L97:   - `session_meta` (first line): `payload.id`, `cwd`, `cli_version`,
L98:     `source` (`"cli"` interactive / `"exec"` headless), git info.
L99:   - `turn_context`: `payload.turn_id`, model context window.
L100:   - `event_msg`: lightweight events (`task_started`, `task_complete`,
L101:     `token_count`, `token_consumption`, `agent_message`, `user_message`,
L102:     `exec_command_end`, …).
L103:   - `response_item`: the conversation content (see Transcript).
L104: 
L105: ## Transcript
L106: 
L107: - Location: the session rollout JSONL itself — every hook payload carries it
L108:   as `transcript_path`.
L109: - Format: JSONL (`response_item` entries hold the conversation).
L110: - User prompt field: `payload.type == "message"` && `payload.role == "user"`,
L111:   text in `payload.content[].input_text`. **Filter out entries whose text
L112:   starts with `<environment_context>`** — the first user entry is harness
L113:   context, not a human prompt (verified).
L114: - Assistant content: `payload.role == "assistant"`, text in
L115:   `payload.content[].output_text` — full real content, no placeholders
L116:   (verified).
L117: - Tool calls: `payload.type == "function_call"` with `name` (runtime tool
L118:   name: `write_file`, `edit_file`, `exec_command`, …), `call_id`
L119:   (`call-<uuid>`), `arguments` (JSON string). Results: `function_call_output`
L120:   keyed by `call_id`.
L121: - Modified files field: derived from `function_call` entries —
L122:   `write_file`/`edit_file` take `path`; `exec_command` takes `command` (parse
L123:   shell redirects with care).
L124: - Token usage field: `event_msg` with `payload.type == "token_count"` carrying
L125:   `payload.info.last_token_usage.{input_tokens, cached_input_tokens,
L126:   output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens, total_tokens}` (per API call) and
L127:   `info.total_token_usage` (cumulative). `info` is null on rate-limit-only
L128:   events.
L129: - Example entry:
L130: 
L131:   ```json
L132:   {"timestamp":"…","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Create a file…"}]}}
L133:   ```
L134: 
L135: ## Data Storage Verification
L136: 
L137: - Session files contain actual assistant content: **YES** (verified — the
L138:   stored `output_text` matches what the TUI displayed, e.g. "done").
L139: - Tool calls recorded with names, inputs, and outputs: **YES** (verified —
L140:   `write_file` with `{"contents":"hello","path":"hello.txt"}`).
L141: - Secondary storage: rollout trace bundles under
L142:   `$SARVAM_HOME/rollout-traces/` (debugging artifacts; not needed for the
L143:   protocol).
L144: - Hook data flow: **VERIFIED** — stdin JSON present for all eight events;
L145:   `transcript_path` resolves to the live native session file.
L146: - Verification method: probe project at a temp dir with capture hooks for all
L147:   8 events; payloads in `testdata/hook-payloads/`; scripted in
L148:   `scripts/verify-sarvam.sh`.
L149: 
L150: ## Protocol Mapping
L151: 
L152: | Subcommand | Native Concept | Implementation Notes | Feasibility |
L153: |-----------|---------------|---------------------|-------------|
L154: | `info` | — | Static metadata | Required |
L155: | `detect` | `sarvam-code` on PATH | Also true when `$SARVAM_HOME` exists | Required |
L156: | `get-session-id` | hook input `session_id` | Echo; generate stub when empty | Required |
L157: | `get-session-dir` | `$SARVAM_HOME/sessions` | Honor `SARVAM_HOME` env | Required |
L158: | `resolve-session-file` | rollout filename suffix | Glob `**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl` under dir; fallback `<dir>/<safe-id>.jsonl` | Required |
L159: | `read-session` | AgentSessionJSON | Round-trip via fallback path | Required |
L160: | `write-session` | AgentSessionJSON | Write to resolved path | Required |
L161: | `read-transcript` | raw rollout bytes | Passthrough | Required |
L162: | `chunk-transcript` | raw bytes | Base64 chunks of `--max-size` | Required |
L163: | `reassemble-transcript` | reverse chunk | Concatenate | Required |
L164: | `format-resume-command` | `sarvam-code resume` | `sarvam-code resume <session-id>` | Required |
L165: | `parse-hook` | native hook JSON → EventJSON | Dual-format: accept native sarvam JSON (has `hook_event_name`) and protocol HookInputJSON (has `hook_type`) | Required |
L166: | `install-hooks` | project `.sarvam/config.toml` | Upsert `[[hooks.*]]` matcher-group entries; `matcher = ".*"` for tool events; plain-`entire` command via PATH guard | If hooks capable |
L167: | `uninstall-hooks` | reverse of install | Remove only entire-owned entries | If hooks capable |
L168: | `are-hooks-installed` | project config check | All installed events present | If hooks capable |
L169: | `get-transcript-position` | file size | Byte offset (transcript is append-only) | If transcript analyzer |
L170: | `extract-modified-files` | `function_call` entries | `write_file`/`edit_file` `path`; `exec_command` shell parsing | If transcript analyzer |
L171: | `extract-prompts` | user messages | `input_text`, drop `<environment_context>` | If transcript analyzer |
L172: | `extract-summary` | — | No native summary in session files → `has_summary=false` | If transcript analyzer |
L173: | `calculate-tokens` | `token_count` events | Sum `last_token_usage` since offset; count non-null `info` for `api_call_count` | If token calculator |
L174: 
L175: ## Selected Capabilities
L176: 
L177: | Capability | Declared | Justification |
L178: |-----------|----------|---------------|
L179: | hooks | true | Native TOML hook config; install/uninstall/is-installed map directly |
L180: | transcript_analyzer | true | Native JSONL transcripts with full content |
L181: | transcript_preparer | false | Native transcript already structured; no preprocessing needed |
L182: | token_calculator | true | `token_count` events carry per-call usage |
L183: | text_generator | false | Would require live model API per invocation; out of scope |
L184: | hook_response_writer | false | Hook stdout already returns to the agent, but the full writer contract is unverified |
L185: | subagent_aware_extractor | false | Subagent threads live in separate rollout files; defer |
L186: | uses_terminal | true | Sarvam Code is an interactive TUI agent |
L187: 
L188: ## Gaps & Limitations
L189: 
L190: - **Headless runs are invisible to hooks.** `sarvam-code exec` never fires
L191:   hooks (verified). Checkpoint capture requires interactive sessions; the e2e
L192:   adapter must drive the TUI through tmux, and `RunPrompt` cannot use exec.
L193: - **One-time interactive bootstrap per repo.** After `install-hooks`, the user
L194:   must (1) trust the directory on first sarvam launch and (2) review + enable
L195:   the hooks in `/hooks`. The `trusted_hash` scheme is opaque, so the binary
L196:   cannot pre-seed hook state; automating it would bypass sarvam's security
L197:   model. Same class of caveat as Grok's `/hooks-trust`.
L198: - **Tool hooks need a matcher.** Declarations for `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`
L199:   must set `matcher` or they silently never fire (verified). The installer
L200:   sets `matcher = ".*"`.
L201: - `extract-summary` returns `has_summary=false`: session files have no
L202:   native summary object (compaction summaries live in trace bundles, not the
L203:   rollout JSONL).
L204: - Interactive-only hook firing also means the compliance suite's hook tests
L205:   validate install/uninstall/parse behavior only — real hook delivery is
L206:   covered by the lifecycle harness.
L207: 
L208: ## Captured Payloads
L209: 
L210: - Verification script: `scripts/verify-sarvam.sh`
L211: - Captures: `testdata/hook-payloads/{SessionStart,UserPromptSubmit,PreToolUse,PostToolUse,PermissionRequest,PreCompact,PostCompact,Stop}.json`
L212: - Verification status: **VERIFIED** (all 8 events captured from live
L213:   sarvam-code 0.58.0 sessions on 2026-11-16)
L214: - Notable differences from docs: the documented `SessionStart` hook config
L215:   example omits the `[[hooks.SessionStart]]` matcher-group header and is
L216:   rejected by the CLI; tool hooks require an explicit `matcher`; hooks do not
L217:   fire in exec mode (docs do not state this).
L218: 
L219: ## E2E Test Prerequisites
L220: 
L221: - Entire CLI binary: `entire` from PATH (`E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` override)
L222: - Agent CLI binary: `sarvam-code`
L223: - Non-interactive prompt command: `sarvam-code exec --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> "<prompt>"` — usable for file-creation assertions only; hooks do NOT fire, so checkpoints require the interactive path
L224: - Interactive mode: supported — `sarvam-code` TUI; drive via tmux
L225: - Expected prompt pattern: the TUI status bar line, e.g. `Flow · (Auto|Ask|Yolo)` — the composer line is `› `
L226: - Timeout multiplier: 2.0 (full agent turns with model latency)
L227: - Bootstrap steps: login already done in the environment; per-repo: the adapter grants directory trust with a headless exec run and pre-seeds `[hooks.state]` (enabled + trusted_hash) with the exact entries a completed `/hooks` review writes — the hashes are derived from the hook commands alone and are stable per sarvam-code version (stale constants fail loudly via the review banner)
L228: - Transient error patterns: `overloaded`, `rate limit`, `429`, `500`, `503`, `econnreset`, `etimedout`, `timeout`
L229: - Lifecycle status (2026-11-16, sarvam-code 0.58.0, entire 0.13.5-nightly): 6 of 8
L230:   scenarios pass end to end (single + multiple prompt checkpoints, detect/enable,
L231:   hooks-installed, session persistence, interactive session).
L232:   `TestLifecycle_RewindPreCommit` and `TestLifecycle_RewindAfterCommit` fail in
L233:   the shared harness at `entire checkpoint rewind --list` — this entire build has
L234:   no `checkpoint rewind` subcommand. The failure occurs before any agent-specific
L235:   assertion and is environment-wide, not sarvam-specific.

L1: # entire-agent-sarvam
L2: 
L3: External agent integration that teaches the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) to work with [Sarvam Code](https://sarvam.ai).
L4: 
L5: Sarvam Code keeps its own durable session transcripts (rollout JSONL under
L6: `$SARVAM_HOME/sessions/`), so Entire checkpoints attach real conversation
L7: content, and `token_count` events feed token usage per checkpoint.
L8: 
L9: ## Capabilities
L10: 
L11: | Capability | Status |
L12: |-----------|--------|
L13: | `hooks` | yes — project `.sarvam/config.toml`, five lifecycle events |
L14: | `transcript_analyzer` | yes — native rollout JSONL |
L15: | `compact_transcript` | yes — projects the rollout into Entire Transcript Format |
L16: | `token_calculator` | yes — per-call usage from `token_count` events |
L17: | `uses_terminal` | yes — Sarvam Code is a TUI agent |
L18: | `text_generator` / `hook_response_writer` / `subagent_aware_extractor` / `transcript_preparer` | no |
L19: 
L20: Events installed: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PreCompact`,
L21: `PostCompact`. Tool and permission events are not installed: Entire has no
L22: event type for them, and the native transcript already records tool calls.
L23: 
L24: ## Build and install
L25: 
L26: ```bash
L27: cd agents/entire-agent-sarvam
L28: mise run build
L29: cp entire-agent-sarvam ~/.local/bin/
L30: ```
L31: 
L32: ## Enable
L33: 
L34: ```bash
L35: cd /path/to/your/repo
L36: entire agent add sarvam
L37: ```
L38: 
L39: `install-hooks` writes the hook declarations into the repo's
L40: `.sarvam/config.toml`. Two sarvam-side gates then apply, both one-time per
L41: repository:
L42: 
L43: 1. **Directory trust.** Sarvam ignores a project config until the directory
L44:    is trusted. The first interactive launch prompts for it — or a single
L45:    headless run (`sarvam-code exec …`) records trust automatically.
L46: 2. **Hook review.** Freshly installed hooks must be trusted and enabled in
L47:    the TUI: open sarvam-code, run `/hooks`, and for each `entire-*` hook
L48:    press `t` (trust) then space (enable). Until then the hooks do not fire
L49:    and Entire records no checkpoints.
L50: 
L51: Hooks fire in **interactive sessions only**. `sarvam-code exec` (headless)
L52: never invokes hooks — checkpoints and transcripts are captured from TUI
L53: sessions.
L54: 
L55: ## Testing
L56: 
L57: ```bash
L58: cd agents/entire-agent-sarvam
L59: mise run test                              # unit tests
L60: external-agents-tests verify ./entire-agent-sarvam   # protocol compliance
L61: 
L62: cd /path/to/repo
L63: E2E_AGENT=sarvam mise run test:e2e:lifecycle  # lifecycle (needs sarvam-code + tmux)
L64: ```
L65: 
L66: The lifecycle adapter drives the interactive TUI through tmux: it trusts the
L67: temp repo with a headless exec run, automates the one-time `/hooks` review,
L68: and sends prompts like a user would. It requires a logged-in `sarvam-code`.
L69: 
L70: See `AGENT.md` for the full research mapping (hook payload schemas, session
L71: file format, trust model) verified against sarvam-code 0.58.0.

(End of file - total 71 lines)

# Sarvam Code — External Agent Research

## Verdict: COMPATIBLE

Sarvam Code has a native TOML-configured lifecycle hook system with JSON
payloads on stdin, durable JSONL session transcripts that carry the full
conversation, and token-usage events inside those transcripts. Every protocol
subcommand maps to a native concept. Two caveats shape the integration:

1. **Hooks fire only in interactive (TUI) sessions.** Headless `sarvam-code
   exec` runs never invoke hooks (verified with a trusted, enabled config).
2. **Project hooks are gated behind a one-time interactive review.** A fresh
   `.sarvam/config.toml` needs (a) directory trust and (b) per-hook trust +
   enable via the `/hooks` TUI screen, which persists to the user config.
   Neither step is automatable from the agent binary (the trust hash scheme is
   opaque), so `install-hooks` writes the declarations and the review is a
   documented bootstrap step.

## Static Checks

| Check | Result | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Binary present | PASS | `/Users/soph/.local/bin/sarvam-code` (installed via PATH) |
| Help available | PASS | `sarvam-code --help`, subcommands: exec, resume, fork, debug, … |
| Version info | PASS | `cli 0.58.0` (`sarvam-code --version`) |
| Hook keywords | PASS | `[hooks]` config table, `/hooks` TUI screen |
| Session keywords | PASS | `resume`, `fork`, `sessions/` directory, `--last` |
| Config directory | PASS | `$SARVAM_HOME` (default `~/.sarvam`); project `.sarvam/` |
| Documentation | PASS | bundled self-knowledge skill tree (hook + session reference) |

## Binary

- Name: `sarvam-code`
- Version: 0.58.0 (verified)
- Install: official installer; binary at `~/.local/bin/sarvam-code`
- Non-interactive prompt: `sarvam-code exec [--skip-git-repo-check] [-C <dir>] "<prompt>"`

## Hook Mechanism (verified against live payloads)

- Config file (project): `<repo>/.sarvam/config.toml` — trust-gated
- Config file (user): `$SARVAM_HOME/config.toml`
- Config format: TOML. Each event key is an **array of matcher groups**:

  ```toml
  [[hooks.SessionStart]]
  [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]]
  type = "command"
  command = "sh -c '…'"
  ```

  The self-knowledge docs' `SessionStart` example omits the matcher-group
  header; without it the CLI fails with `invalid type: map, expected a
  sequence` (reproduced). Handler fields: `type` (`"command"`), `command`,
  optional `timeout` (seconds), `async`, `statusMessage`. Tool events
  additionally **require** `matcher` (a regex matched against the model-facing
  tool name, e.g. `Bash`, `Write`); a missing matcher silently never fires.

- Hook names and protocol mapping:

  | Native Hook Name | When It Fires | Protocol Event Type |
  |-----------------|---------------|---------------------|
  | `SessionStart` | session begins / first turn starts | 1 = SessionStart |
  | `UserPromptSubmit` | user submits a prompt | 2 = TurnStart |
  | `Stop` | agent ends its turn | 3 = TurnEnd |
  | `PreCompact` | before context compaction | 4 = Compaction |
  | `PostCompact` | after context compaction | 4 = Compaction |
  | `PreToolUse` | before a tool call (needs matcher) | null (not forwarded) |
  | `PostToolUse` | after a tool call (needs matcher) | null (not forwarded) |
  | `PermissionRequest` | permission approval needed | null (not forwarded) |

- Hook input format: JSON on stdin; the command's stdout is returned to the
  agent as context; non-zero exit can block the action (PreToolUse,
  PermissionRequest).
- Trust model (verified):
  - The project layer loads only after the directory is trusted. First
    interactive run prompts; accepting writes
    `[projects."<abs path>"] trust_level = "trusted"` to the **user** config.
    Until then the project config (hooks included) is silently ignored.
  - Each hook additionally needs interactive review: `/hooks` → select →
    `t` (trust) → space (enable). This persists
    `[hooks.state."<project-config>:<event_snake>:<matcher-idx>:<hook-idx>"]`
    entries with `enabled` and `trusted_hash` (sha256, scheme opaque) to the
    **user** config. Not reproducible offline (brute-forced several
    serializations; no match), so the installer cannot pre-seed it.

## Session Management

- Session directory: `$SARVAM_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/` (local start date).
  Override root via `SARVAM_HOME` env. Archived sessions move to
  `$SARVAM_HOME/archived_sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`.
- Session files: one JSONL per run:
  `rollout-<YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss>-<thread_id>.jsonl` where `<thread_id>` is
  the session UUID.
- Session ID source: hook input `session_id` (== thread UUID == the rollout
  filename suffix == `session_meta.payload.id`).
- Session file format: JSONL, one object per line with `timestamp` + `type`:
  - `session_meta` (first line): `payload.id`, `cwd`, `cli_version`,
    `source` (`"cli"` interactive / `"exec"` headless), git info.
  - `turn_context`: `payload.turn_id`, model context window.
  - `event_msg`: lightweight events (`task_started`, `task_complete`,
    `token_count`, `token_consumption`, `agent_message`, `user_message`,
    `exec_command_end`, …).
  - `response_item`: the conversation content (see Transcript).

## Transcript

- Location: the session rollout JSONL itself — every hook payload carries it
  as `transcript_path`.
- Format: JSONL (`response_item` entries hold the conversation).
- User prompt field: `payload.type == "message"` && `payload.role == "user"`,
  text in `payload.content[].input_text`. **Filter out entries whose text
  starts with `<environment_context>`** — the first user entry is harness
  context, not a human prompt (verified).
- Assistant content: `payload.role == "assistant"`, text in
  `payload.content[].output_text` — full real content, no placeholders
  (verified).
- Tool calls: `payload.type == "function_call"` with `name` (runtime tool
  name: `write_file`, `edit_file`, `exec_command`, …), `call_id`
  (`call-<uuid>`), `arguments` (JSON string). Results: `function_call_output`
  keyed by `call_id`.
- Modified files field: derived from `function_call` entries —
  `write_file`/`edit_file` take `path`; `exec_command` takes `command` (parse
  shell redirects with care).
- Token usage field: `event_msg` with `payload.type == "token_count"` carrying
  `payload.info.last_token_usage.{input_tokens, cached_input_tokens,
  output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens, total_tokens}` (per API call) and
  `info.total_token_usage` (cumulative). `info` is null on rate-limit-only
  events.
- Example entry:

  ```json
  {"timestamp":"…","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Create a file…"}]}}
  ```

## Data Storage Verification

- Session files contain actual assistant content: **YES** (verified — the
  stored `output_text` matches what the TUI displayed, e.g. "done").
- Tool calls recorded with names, inputs, and outputs: **YES** (verified —
  `write_file` with `{"contents":"hello","path":"hello.txt"}`).
- Secondary storage: rollout trace bundles under
  `$SARVAM_HOME/rollout-traces/` (debugging artifacts; not needed for the
  protocol).
- Hook data flow: **VERIFIED** — stdin JSON present for all eight events;
  `transcript_path` resolves to the live native session file.
- Verification method: probe project at a temp dir with capture hooks for all
  8 events; payloads in `testdata/hook-payloads/`; scripted in
  `scripts/verify-sarvam.sh`.

## Protocol Mapping

| Subcommand | Native Concept | Implementation Notes | Feasibility |
|-----------|---------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `info` | — | Static metadata | Required |
| `detect` | `sarvam-code` on PATH | Also true when `$SARVAM_HOME` exists | Required |
| `get-session-id` | hook input `session_id` | Echo; generate stub when empty | Required |
| `get-session-dir` | `$SARVAM_HOME/sessions` | Honor `SARVAM_HOME` env | Required |
| `resolve-session-file` | rollout filename suffix | Glob `**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl` under dir; fallback `<dir>/<safe-id>.jsonl` | Required |
| `read-session` | AgentSessionJSON | Round-trip via fallback path | Required |
| `write-session` | AgentSessionJSON | Store path writes normally; a rollout-shaped ref is created once when absent (restore), never when present | Required |
| `read-transcript` | raw rollout bytes | Passthrough | Required |
| `chunk-transcript` | raw bytes | Base64 chunks of `--max-size` | Required |
| `reassemble-transcript` | reverse chunk | Concatenate | Required |
| `format-resume-command` | `sarvam-code resume` | `sarvam-code resume <session-id>` | Required |
| `parse-hook` | native hook JSON → EventJSON | Dual-format: accept native sarvam JSON (has `hook_event_name`) and protocol HookInputJSON (has `hook_type`) | Required |
| `install-hooks` | project `.sarvam/config.toml` | Upsert `[[hooks.*]]` matcher-group entries; `matcher = ".*"` for tool events; plain-`entire` command via PATH guard | If hooks capable |
| `uninstall-hooks` | reverse of install | Remove only entire-owned entries | If hooks capable |
| `are-hooks-installed` | project config check | All installed events present | If hooks capable |
| `get-transcript-position` | physical line count | Line index consumed so far; a torn final line is excluded so late bytes are not skipped | If transcript analyzer |
| `extract-modified-files` | `function_call` entries | Write-tool allowlist: `write_file`/`edit_file` `path`; `exec_command` (`cmd`, older releases `command`) shell redirects; read-only tools excluded | If transcript analyzer |
| `extract-prompts` | user messages | `input_text`, drop `<environment_context>` | If transcript analyzer |
| `extract-summary` | — | No native summary in session files → `has_summary=false` | If transcript analyzer |
| `calculate-tokens` | `token_count` events | Delta of cumulative `total_token_usage` since offset (input bucket excludes the cached share); an advancing total is one API call; torn final line skipped | If token calculator |

## Selected Capabilities

| Capability | Declared | Justification |
|-----------|----------|---------------|
| hooks | true | Native TOML hook config; install/uninstall/is-installed map directly |
| transcript_analyzer | true | Native JSONL transcripts with full content |
| transcript_preparer | false | Native transcript already structured; no preprocessing needed |
| token_calculator | true | `token_count` events carry per-call usage |
| text_generator | false | Would require live model API per invocation; out of scope |
| hook_response_writer | false | Hook stdout already returns to the agent, but the full writer contract is unverified |
| subagent_aware_extractor | false | Subagent threads live in separate rollout files; defer |
| uses_terminal | true | Sarvam Code is an interactive TUI agent |

## Gaps & Limitations

- **Headless runs are invisible to hooks.** `sarvam-code exec` never fires
  hooks (verified). Checkpoint capture requires interactive sessions; the e2e
  adapter must drive the TUI through tmux, and `RunPrompt` cannot use exec.
- **One-time interactive bootstrap per repo.** After `install-hooks`, the user
  must (1) trust the directory on first sarvam launch and (2) review + enable
  the hooks in `/hooks`. The `trusted_hash` scheme is opaque, so the binary
  cannot pre-seed hook state; automating it would bypass sarvam's security
  model. Same class of caveat as Grok's `/hooks-trust`.
- **Tool hooks need a matcher.** Declarations for `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`
  must set `matcher` or they silently never fire (verified). The installer
  sets `matcher = ".*"`.
- `extract-summary` returns `has_summary=false`: session files have no
  native summary object (compaction summaries live in trace bundles, not the
  rollout JSONL).
- Interactive-only hook firing also means the compliance suite's hook tests
  validate install/uninstall/parse behavior only — real hook delivery is
  covered by the lifecycle harness.

## Captured Payloads

- Verification script: `scripts/verify-sarvam.sh`
- Captures: `testdata/hook-payloads/{SessionStart,UserPromptSubmit,PreToolUse,PostToolUse,PermissionRequest,PreCompact,PostCompact,Stop}.json`
- Verification status: **VERIFIED** (all 8 events captured from live
  sarvam-code 0.58.0 sessions on 2026-11-16)
- Notable differences from docs: the documented `SessionStart` hook config
  example omits the `[[hooks.SessionStart]]` matcher-group header and is
  rejected by the CLI; tool hooks require an explicit `matcher`; hooks do not
  fire in exec mode (docs do not state this).

## E2E Test Prerequisites

- Entire CLI binary: `entire` from PATH (`E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` override)
- Agent CLI binary: `sarvam-code`
- Non-interactive prompt command: `sarvam-code exec --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> "<prompt>"` — usable for file-creation assertions only; hooks do NOT fire, so checkpoints require the interactive path
- Interactive mode: supported — `sarvam-code` TUI; drive via tmux
